response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), s AS (SELECT rating, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(s.cnt) AS total_count, AVG(s.share) AS avg_kept_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_excess_share FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share

assumptions.assumption: "Count the films rented" per rating is the number of rental records (each rental counts once, so a film rented several times counts several times), after inner joining to inventory and film.
Ratings with NULL values are treated as their own group if present; the verified data shows 5 non-null ratings, so this does not matter.

alternatives.interpretation: Count distinct films rented per rating (each film counted once regardless of how many times it was rented).
alternatives.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT f.film_id) AS cnt FROM rental r JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id JOIN film f ON f.film_id = i.film_id GROUP BY f.rating), s AS (SELECT rating, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM c), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(s.cnt) AS total_count, AVG(s.share) AS avg_kept_share, AVG(s.share - a.avg_share) AS avg_excess_share FROM s CROSS JOIN a WHERE s.share > a.avg_share
